title: Gaussian moment identity for a family of linear functionals
statement: Let $n\ge 0$ and let $L$ assign to each $x\in\mathbb R^n$ a continuous linear functional $L(x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, continuously in $x$. Then the nonnegative extended Gaussian integral of $|L(z_1)(z_2)|$ over independent standard Gaussian vectors $z_1,z_2\in\mathbb R^n$ equals $2\varphi(0)$ times the nonnegative extended Gaussian integral of $\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n (L(x)e_i)^2}$ over $x\in\mathbb R^n$, where $e_i$ are the coordinate unit vectors and $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
hypotheses_covered: $L(x)$ is a continuous linear functional for each $x\in\mathbb R^n$
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. If $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathcal L(\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R)$ is continuous, put $|L(x)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i(L(x)e_i)^2}$. Then $\mathbb E|L(X)Y|=(\mathbb E|L(X)|_2)\,2\varphi(0)$ as nonnegative extended integrals, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
